## d75d93612b90

**Reproduced contract defect.** Generator SHA-256 `60dcdb11c6ca0ff6e30b8dcb3706230a869fbfa8338ff0cbc170b1a4d53453c5` accepts out-of-domain `direction="diagonal"` and silently executes the `right` branch; its self-check reports no error. An unknown `typo_axis` is also accepted and ignored.

**Possible shortcut.** In all 240 sampled inputs across easy/default/hard/challenge, there was exactly one isolated orange component and it was always the fixed 2×2 block at coordinates `(1,1)`–`(2,2)`. A solver can preserve that fixed location and transform the only other orange object without learning isolation from absence of gray contact.

**Concrete counterexample.** `checks/audit/d75d93612b90/finding.json` moves the isolated 2×2 orange object to `(0,3)`–`(1,4)` while keeping a separate gray-contacted orange block. The target validator accepts it. Canonical Racket rule hash `eca2fe4b3b91` preserves the moved isolated object orange; the `fixed_top_left_isolation` rival leaves those four cells gray. The input is lawful for the semantic isolation rule but outside this generator's fixed-location subdistribution.

**Patch status.** Findings only; this audit target was left unchanged.
